Deltas the proposal must absorb: (A) CLAUDE.md:364 conditions bind any RDI DRBG — (b) ≥246-bit state treated as secret, S-SRAM only, zeroized on lock/tamper/brownout; (c) ONE consumer per generator instance and it must NOT live in `rng.rs` (`negative_no_software_prng_seed_in_rng_module` gate) — so the RDI generator cannot be shared with the consumption-mask xorshift; (d) a MEASURED, bounded, non-dominant fallback rate in the evidence record; (e) no SP 800-90A 'approved DRBG' claim (ChaCha is not one of the three mechanisms); (f) the FSBL's deterministic delay stub must be covered or recorded as a contract-vs-code gap. (B) Owner comment on #805 2026-10-09 narrowed the DRBG's justification: the fill-internal starvation (31 identical replayed delays per `rng::fill`, #832) has a TRNG-only fix that landed as `fi_delay_pool.rs` on master, so the carve-out's remaining purpose is exactly the RDI case — but the owner's own open sub-question 5 ('our sensitive ops are multi-second C10 signs; per-ms jitter value deserves an argument, not an assumption') is unanswered; the proposal's rationale should answer it. (C) Item (3) 'failed TRNG draw fails the operation, not halt' is #835's position, but the recorded owner quote on #834 (2026-10-09) is 'if the RNG fails, we shouldn't fallback. It should error out' and dd901592 implements a silent HALT (arm 4); #835 (two blind reviewers) found that halt is reachable before the conditioning-reset recovery runs and from the ~1 s consumption-mask SysTick reseed. Which sink (halt vs. refuse-operation) is a pending owner adjudication on #835, not settled. (D) #805 already records the TE phase-lock hazard (`sync_to_scanout` 18 µs strobe poll; #783's EXTI latch mitigates) and recommends a separate lower-priority timer rather than extending the highest-priority SysTick ISR — the proposal's TIM2/TIM3 choice should note TIM2_CH1 (iota2) / TIM3_CH1 (pq1) are already the consumption-mask PWM timers (`sau.rs:316-341`). (E) `e2e-test` makes `wait_random` a no-op (fi.rs:91); any RDI must carry the same fence and a `prodtest`-style fence that cannot reach a shipping image (#805 sub-question 4).

feasible.reason: The proposal is sound and feasible on pq1 with no hardware change: the secure world already runs a 1 kHz secure SysTick (secure/src/main.rs `SysTick`, `setup_systick` :857, highest priority) that does per-tick work including a TRNG-reseeded xorshift32 (consumption-mask), so an RDI hook is a small ISR addition, not a new timer. The stated threat is real on this tree: jitter exists only at `crate::fi::wait_random()` call sites, master and this branch still carry the `byte_nonsecret(FI_DELAY_LAST_GOOD)` reuse arm (fi.rs:58-72; `git show master:secure/src/fi.rs` confirms), and the #832/#834 rework lives only on perf/flash-opt-level-z. An always-on floating-mean RDI does raise the cost of event-triggered glitching on every path longer than ~1 ms (the multi-second C10 sign, SE tunnel setup, LCD windows), and a DRBG-fed delay source removes the TRNG-latch switch that collapses delays to a constant. It is a cost-raiser, not a preventer (pattern/power-trace triggers immediately before a gate are unaffected, as for Trezor), which the proposal honestly labels 'parity'. Cost M and P1 are defensible for parts (1)(2)(4); part (3) as literally written (fallible wait_random at ~800 sites) is L, see corrections. The budget arithmetic (≤510 cycles/ms ≈ 0.3 % worst case) checks out and the TE-window risk is overstated: +~90 µs over a 27.9 ms write against a 3.5 ms margin needs no masking.
feasible.corrections: 1) Host it on the existing secure SysTick, not TIM2/TIM3: the ISR already exists (main.rs `SysTick`) and TIM3 on pq1 is the consumption-mask PWM; adding a second timer is unnecessary flash and a second ISR priority to reason about. 2) 'Refresh on USB packet receipt' is not realisable: USB OTG is NS-owned (sau.rs), so the secure world cannot see packets; the only secure-observable refresh points are NSC veneer entry (nsc/mod.rs dispatcher) and S-world button edges (ui::px::lcd::systick_sample). Every meaningful USB packet ends in a veneer call anyway, so the loss is nil; say so instead of promising a USB hook. 3) The RDI gives zero jitter in the first ~1 ms after a trigger (a tick only lands in a sub-ms window with probability ≈ window/1 ms); the 'USB-triggered dispatch before the first wait_random' gate is NOT covered by RDI alone. Add a session-delay-length wait at dispatcher entry (cheap, and a compromised NS can anyway toggle a trigger right before the veneer call), and keep per-site wait_random for the pattern-trigger case. 4) The ISR must never draw from the TRNG directly: hw::rng holds a driver lock (#835 H5) and the consumption-mask reseed already draws from the ISR, which is exactly the path #835 C1 shows halting; reseed the DRBG from thread mode at veneer entry/exit, so the RDI never contends. A ChaCha8/20 block per 64 draws is ~20-30 cycles/byte amortised; do not use the AES/SAES peripheral from the ISR (contention with main-thread wrap/KDF). Flash cost ~1-3 KB on a slot already 76,949 B over under ui-px; flag it. 5) The 'No software PRNG' line in CLAUDE.md is the #805 blocker, but the tree already ships a software xorshift32 in the SysTick ISR for the mask duty; the proposal should cite that precedent and ask for an explicit owner carve-out for non-secret countermeasure randomness rather than imply the DRBG is uncontroversial. 6) 'RDI switches to fault on TRNG error' is the wrong shape: with a DRBG the ISR never observes TRNG errors; a failed thread-mode reseed should set a sticky 'countermeasure degraded' flag that fails every release gate (sign release, PIN commit in pin_attempts_bump BEFORE the quadword write, flash writes), which is the #835 option-2 outcome without making ~800 wait_random sites fallible. Done that way part (3) stays M; done as per-site fallibility it is L. 7) Honest framing: RDI defeats trigger-plus-fixed-delay and cross-session averaging, not pattern-triggered FI; with std ≈ 74·√N cycles it is a ~1000x per-shot cost increase on a 1 s path, not prevention. 8) Keep RDI off under e2e-test (wait_random is already a no-op there) and re-baseline test-key-speed; bench DWT numbers gain ±0.3 %, no action needed. 9) The TE-sync code (#780) lives in the pq1-uiconform worktree, not in PQSigner_OS master; the masking claim should be verified there, but the arithmetic says no mask is needed.

vendor-claim.reason: The core precedent claim holds: Trezor ships an always-on 1 ms floating-mean Random Delay Interrupt, default-enabled in kernel and secmon, with session_delay refresh on USB packets and a fault-trap on a corrupted enable flag; novelty='parity' is correct (no evidence any other vendor ships a periodic RDI; TF-M and the Sass paper only do call-site delays; Ledger BOLOS is closed with no public RDI evidence, but Ledger Donjon's FDTC23 talk literally recommends combining double verification with jitter). Repo evidence is accurate (last-good TRNG reuse live on master; no-reuse rework only on perf/flash-opt-level-z; #805/#834/#835 open). Several precedent details are wrong or overstated (date, SMCALL refresh semantics, button-edge refresh, bootloader scope, source support) — these are corrections, not a refutation.
vendor-claim.corrections: (1) DATE: Trezor's periodic RDI landed 2020-02-26 (commit c461692f3a 'core: implement random delay interrupts', O. Vejpustek), not 2019; the 2019 commits (f677a0f0db, e6ee13e798) are call-site wait_random only. Say 'shipped RDI since 2020 (wait_random since 2019)'. (2) REFRESH SITES: smcall_dispatch.c:161-167 is NOT a refresh on every SMCALL/NSC dispatch — it is the dedicated SMCALL_RANDOM_DELAYS_REFRESH_RDI case, reached only via the NS stub smcall_stubs.c:160-162, whose sole callers are usb.c:728 (DataIn) and usb.c:748 (DataOut) under #ifdef RDI. Trezor refreshes session_delay ONLY on USB data events; it does not refresh on syscall entry or button edges. The proposal's 'refresh on NSC veneer entry + button edge' therefore goes slightly beyond Trezor (minor 'beyond' element inside an otherwise-parity item). (3) SCOPE: Trezor's bootloader never starts RDI (bootloader/main.c:319 calls only random_delays_init(); no start_rdi in bootloader/boardloader) — RDI runs in kernel/secmon only. Any claim of 'Trezor-parity' for an FSBL-side RDI would be beyond, not parity. (4) BUILD GATING: the RDI define is produced by the Cargo feature sec/rdi (random_delays/build.rs:7-9 -> -DRDI), listed in the automatically-derived `default` set of kernel/Cargo.toml:97-106 and secmon/Cargo.toml:75-83 (SCons FEATURE_FLAGS 'RDI': True until a4b25c3174, 2026-08-04). (5) TREZOR WART NOT TO COPY: drbg_random8 returns the constant 128 when its atomic lock is contended (random_delays.c:72-85) — the proposal's DRBG must not reproduce a contention-constant arm, since that is the same class of defect as the #834 reuse arm. (6) LEDGER: no public evidence that BOLOS/ST33 runs a software RDI; the only Ledger-attributable support is the FDTC23 DS28C36 talk (Abdellatif & Hériveaux, Ledger Donjon, slide 28) and the GreHack24 'Jitter' bullet listed under chip-provider physical countermeasures. State 'Ledger Donjon recommends jitter' rather than 'Ledger ships it'. (7) SOURCES: Sass USENIX'23 (µ-Glitch) supports 'single trigger -> coordinated multi-fault' but its countermeasure (§7, lines 1233-1262 of the text) is compile-time/call-site random delay before duplicate-register assignments, arguing a 0-9 cycle site-local delay cuts MFI success 100x — it does not argue for a global RDI and does not support the 'profiled linear path between sites' rationale; cite Clavier/Coron/Dabbous + Tunstall/Benoit (as random_delays.h:36-41 does) for the floating-mean argument instead. The TF-M doc provides only call-site fih_delay_random() (HIGH profile), no periodic interrupt. (8) REPO FRAMING: timeout.rs:1-27 documents a SysTick-driven ~1 ms secure tick (tick_verified) already in place, so the natural host is that SysTick slot; TIM2 (iota2) / TIM3 (pq1) are already consumed by the consumption-mask PWM (consumption_mask.rs:30-31), not free. wait_random is a no-op under e2e-test (fi.rs:87-91); an RDI must mirror that gate or bench/e2e timings and the pq1 DWT measurements drift. #805 is currently labelled priority:medium / surface:clear-signing, not fi/P1 — relabel if this item is adopted. (9) Repo evidence otherwise confirmed: fi.rs:58-59,72 last-good reuse on master and feat/pq1-board-target; dd901592 (no-reuse, fi_delay_pool) is only on perf/flash-opt-level-z (git branch --contains); #834 OPEN priority:high, #835 OPEN priority:critical.
